To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
policy is a key factor in the success of a system selection and implementation, and that the impact of the policy is to legitimize power, establish discourse and limit resistance.

1) resistance is a natural response to change, 2) policy is a tool that can be used to overcome resistance, and 3) policy can be a double-edged sword that can both help and hinder system implementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of power and policy on the implementation of information systems.
the issue of resistance and the impact of policy on resistance in systems implementation.
understanding the impact policy has in the implementation of new systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implementation of a new system is not a simple process and the resistance to a new system is a complex issue.
resistance is a complex and dynamic issue and the implementation of policy can be used as a tool to diminish opposition.
the policy enacted by the University of South Australia (UniSA) legitimised power, established discourse and limited resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
policy is the most powerful weapon in the armoury for system implementation and that resistance can be overcome by the use of policy to legitimise the system.
resistance can only be diminished if it can be legitimised.
policy has a strong influence on the selection and implementation process of a new system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of policy is significant and must be taken into account when considering systems selection and implementation.
policy can be used to influence system selection and implementation and can be an effective tool in overcoming resistance to new systems.
the implementation of a system is a political process and policy is a powerful weapon in the arsenal of the implementor.
